segments.t: In his office at ASK, majority shareholder Hicham Janowski hands Andréa Martel an expensive designer dress. Eager to secure actor Fabrice Luchini, Hicham pushes Andréa to wear the outfit tonight, but she refuses to be manipulated. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
Sérieusement Hicham, tout avance très bien.
Fais-moi confiance pour ce dossier.
Toute cette pression ne m'aide pas.
J'ai un cadeau pour toi.
Ouvre la boîte tout de suite.
On n'a pas encore gagné.
Mets cette robe ce soir.
Essaie-la maintenant devant moi.
Non, je ne l'essaie pas maintenant!
Nous sommes de vieux camarades d'école.
Il n'est pas question d'enfiler ça.
Très bien. Ne lâche pas Luchini.
Je ne veux pas avoir l'air idiot.
D'accord, je gère la situation.
Now let's break down the scene step by step. Listen to each line, followed by its meaning and a short explanation.
Sérieusement Hicham, tout avance très bien.
'Seriously Hicham, everything is progressing very well.' Andréa starts with a cognate meaning 'seriously', then adds a handy chunk meaning 'everything is going well'. In French, it sounds perfect.
Fais-moi confiance pour ce dossier.
'Trust me with this file.' She uses an informal command meaning 'make me trust', followed by a cognate. This is standard in French.
Toute cette pression ne m'aide pas.
'All this pressure does not help me.' In the negative, the action 'help' is sandwiched between two small pieces. A nice sentence in French.
J'ai un cadeau pour toi.
'I have a gift for you.' Hicham uses the casual 'you' at the end, showing his overly familiar attitude. A great expression in French.
Ouvre la boîte tout de suite.
'Open the box right away.' He gives an informal command to open, followed by a handy chunk meaning 'immediately'. You can say this in French.
On n'a pas encore gagné.
'We have not won yet.' Unlike English, this relies on the everyday spoken piece meaning 'we', paired with 'not yet'. In French, this is widely used.
Mets cette robe ce soir.
'Wear this dress tonight.' He gives another casual command, finishing with a handy chunk meaning 'this evening'. The French love this expression.
Essaie-la maintenant devant moi.
'Try it on now in front of me.' You'll hear an informal command to try, with a handy chunk meaning 'in front of'. In French, it fits perfectly.
Non, je ne l'essaie pas maintenant!
'No, I am not trying it on now!' Andréa forcefully refuses, dropping the object 'it' right before the action. A nice way to say it in French.
Nous sommes de vieux camarades d'école.
'We are old schoolmates.' He tries to justify himself using that everyday spoken 'we' again, joined by 'old'. In French, it is a great choice.
Il n'est pas question d'enfiler ça.
'There is no question of slipping this on.' You can say this opening expression to shut down a demand with absolute authority. The French find this natural.
Très bien. Ne lâche pas Luchini.
'Very well. Do not let go of Luchini.' Hicham backs down, using a negative casual command meaning 'do not let go'. In French, this sounds very fluent.
Je ne veux pas avoir l'air idiot.
'I do not want to look foolish.' The second half uses an idiom literally meaning 'to have the air', followed by a cognate. The French use this structure often.
D'accord, je gère la situation.

'All right, I am managing the situation.' She takes control with a handy chunk meaning 'okay', followed by the action 'I manage'. In French, this phrasing is common. Now let's listen to the entire exchange once more from beginning to end.
Sérieusement Hicham, tout avance très bien.
Fais-moi confiance pour ce dossier.
Toute cette pression ne m'aide pas.
J'ai un cadeau pour toi.
Ouvre la boîte tout de suite.
On n'a pas encore gagné.
Mets cette robe ce soir.
Essaie-la maintenant devant moi.
Non, je ne l'essaie pas maintenant!
Nous sommes de vieux camarades d'école.
Il n'est pas question d'enfiler ça.
Très bien. Ne lâche pas Luchini.
Je ne veux pas avoir l'air idiot.
D'accord, je gère la situation.
Andréa firmly puts Hicham in his place while keeping her focus on signing Fabrice Luchini. Remember the strong French expression for a flat refusal: il n'est pas question de. See you next time!
Au revoir!
